Watts made this hymn from Psalm 46, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble. 2Therefore we will not fear, though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas, 3though their waters roar and foam and the mountains quake in the surge. Selah 4There is a river whose streams delight the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells. … 7 more verses PSALM 46 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 46
God is the refuge of his saints, When storms of sharp distress invade; Ere we can offer our complaints Behold him present with his aid. STANZA I
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 1. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
